parts.transcript: S3: Daniel & Fiona plan a class debate with their tutor. Fiona is keen because a friend did one at secondary school and got a lot out of it = talked about debating with a friend (21=C). Advantage: helps people study all sides / work out what they believe = form opinions (22=A). Topic: they brainstorm a shortlist and students vote = students select one of their suggestions (23=B). Key to success: use an issue students already have strong opinions about = a topic that really involves them (24=A). Two teams = saves time for main speakers on research = share out preparation work (25=C). Lecturer agrees to read the essays and give feedback = comment on students' written work (26=A). Meeting actions: procedures = hand out a summary of key points (27=B, chosen over the board); body language = photocopy of an article with diagrams (28=D); accessing resources = ask students for their own suggestions (29=A, over a compiled list); asking/answering questions = put points on the board (30=C, over a demonstration).

parts.title: Crisis Communication Theory
parts.transcript: S4: lecture on crisis communication theory. Some ask why not just use logic (31) instead of theory; much crisis advice is just a guess (32) that theory/research can test. Three crisis types: victim (e.g. caused by a rumour, 33); accidental (external factors); preventable (resulting from a mistake, 34, within the organisation). Basic two-part response: give info to prevent harm + communicate the action (35) planned to prevent another crisis. Strategies to shape thinking: diminish - provide convincing proof (36) it's not so bad; give excuses (not intentional -> seen as accident). Protect reputation: first reduce negative (37) opinions; rebuild strategies when there's a severe threat (38) to reputation; offer an apology (39) for minor problems; in serious cases offer compensation (40).
parts.formContent:
Crisis Communication Theory

Why do we need theory?

  • Some people think using is better than theory
  • But a lot of advice is simply a

Types of crisis

  • The organisation can be a victim – e.g. due to a
  • Crisis can be accidental – caused by external factors
  • Crisis can be preventable – resulting from a in the organization

Suggested response for all crises

  • Give information to prevent any more damage
  • Communicate what is to be taken

Strategies to influence people’s thinking

  • Diminish the crisis
    • provide that the crisis is not so bad
  • Give excuses for the crisis
    • highlight that it was not intentional

Protecting the organisation’s reputation

  • Initial objective is to lessen opinions
  • Rebuild strategies are important when:
    • there is a serious to the organisation’s reputation
    • the impact of the crisis needs lessening
